citation: City of Chicago, Commission on Chicago Landmarks. "Site of the Sauganash Hotel/Wigwam." Designated 6 November 2002. lanId 1417.
note: Places the Sauganash site at the south-east corner of Lake Street and Wacker Drive (historically Market Street), now 191 N Wacker. Corroborates the Lake and Market location independently of the narrative sources. It also carries the Wigwam: built on the Sauganash site in 1860, where the Republican convention nominated Abraham Lincoln (read 2026-10-16 for a time-stream caption, T-2611).
access_notes: chicago.gov returns 403 to automated fetchers; open in a browser. Read 2026-10-16 (T-2611): the landmark page answered and was read in full. It gives 'Sauganash built 1831, destroyed 1851; Wigwam built 1860, destroyed 1867', and says 'The Wigwam, constructed on the same site nine years later, was home to the 1860 Republican National Convention. It was at this historic convention that Abraham Lincoln was nominated as the Republican candidate for president.'
